debate-on-annual-budget-statement.title: Parliament debates Budget 2026
debate-on-annual-budget-statement.what_it_is: A parliamentary debate on Budget 2026, with MPs speaking and the Prime Minister responding to clarifications.
debate-on-annual-budget-statement.why_it_matters: MPs said Budget 2026 continues one-off support such as CDC vouchers and utilities rebates, and strengthens CPF top-ups and higher contribution rates for seniors. They also said it raises the monthly household income threshold for student care fee assistance to $6,500 and lowers PARF rebates by 45% with a $30,000 cap. The transcript records many further proposals, but does not state that they have been adopted.

an-economy-of-the-future-that-works-for-.title: Motion on Singapore's economic future, amended and agreed to
an-economy-of-the-future-that-works-for-.what_it_is: A Motion moved by Mr Kenneth Tiong and seconded by Assoc Prof Jamus Lim, proposing principles for a more equal and inclusive economy and an economic engine driven by local companies, domestic demand and Singaporeans venturing abroad, which was debated and amended.
an-economy-of-the-future-that-works-for-.why_it_matters: The amended Motion records the House's belief in a more equal and inclusive economy and an economy powered by dynamic local companies, global enterprises, healthy domestic and external demand, and Singaporeans and Singaporean capital venturing abroad. The transcript does not state any direct change to law or schemes from the Motion itself. The record does not set out the practical impact.

land-transport-and-related-matters-bill.title: Land Transport and Related Matters Bill, Second Reading debate
land-transport-and-related-matters-bill.what_it_is: A Second Reading debate on the Land Transport and Related Matters Bill, an omnibus Bill by the Ministry of Transport and Ministry of Home Affairs that amends road traffic, active mobility, ERP 2.0, speed limiter and related laws.
land-transport-and-related-matters-bill.why_it_matters: The Bill decriminalises missed ERP charges and makes the On-Board Unit mandatory for all Singapore-registered vehicles from 1 January 2027. It lowers the speed limit for mobility vehicles on public paths to six kilometres an hour from 1 June 2026, requires a Certificate of Medical Need for mobility scooter users on public paths, and introduces registration and penalties. It also raises penalties for illegal vehicle modifications and unregistered or deregistered vehicles, and updates speed limiter offences.

committee-of-supply-head-k-ministry-of-e.title: Committee of Supply debate on the Ministry of Education budget
committee-of-supply-head-k-ministry-of-e.what_it_is: A Committee of Supply debate on Head K, the Ministry of Education, with Members moving cuts and the Minister and Ministers of State responding.
committee-of-supply-head-k-ministry-of-e.why_it_matters: The debate records changes to primary and secondary education, including the GEP refresh, a single Post-Secondary Admissions Exercise from 2028, Higher Mother Tongue eligibility from Secondary 1, and more financial assistance for lower- to middle-income students from Academic Year 2026. It also records reviews of Primary 1 registration, class sizes, milestone exams and DSA, and a salary review for educators.

committee-of-supply-head-s-ministry-of-m.title: Committee of Supply debate on Manpower Ministry budget and labour policies
committee-of-supply-head-s-ministry-of-m.what_it_is: A Committee of Supply debate on Head S (Manpower) of the Estimates, opened by Ms Yeo Wan Ling moving a $100 reduction amendment, with MPs raising labour policy proposals and ministers responding.
committee-of-supply-head-s-ministry-of-m.why_it_matters: The transcript records planned changes including adding eight occupations to the NTS-OL in 2026, raising EP and S Pass qualifying salaries and the Local Qualifying Salary, extending GRIT to the 2026 cohort, and expanding the Overseas Markets Immersion Programme. It also records proposals from MPs on retrenchment benefits, jobseeker support, caregiver leave, and wage thresholds, but does not state that these proposals will be adopted.

health-information-bill.title: Health Information Bill Second Reading debate
health-information-bill.what_it_is: A Second Reading debate on the Health Information Bill, which requires licensed healthcare providers and retail pharmacies to contribute key health information to the National Electronic Health Record and sets rules for access, sharing and safeguards.
health-information-bill.why_it_matters: The Bill requires all licensed healthcare providers and retail pharmacies to contribute key health information to NEHR, so a patient's records can follow them across providers. It allows patients to restrict access, while critical allergies and vaccination records remain visible, and prohibits access for employment or insurance purposes. The Minister says the Bill is intended to take effect from early 2027.

singapore-sports-council-amendment-bill.title: Singapore Sports Council (Amendment) Bill at Second Reading
singapore-sports-council-amendment-bill.what_it_is: A Bill at Second Reading to amend the Singapore Sports Council Act, expanding SportSG's functions to include physical fitness activities, mind sports and e-sports, and updating its powers over standards, institutions and athlete support.
singapore-sports-council-amendment-bill.why_it_matters: The Bill expands what is legally recognised as sport to include mind sports and e-sports and physical fitness activities, and gives SportSG powers to set standards and establish athlete-training institutions. It also recognises the Singapore National Paralympic Council as a key partner and increases the maximum SportSG Board size from 15 to 25. The Minister said the changes are to empower SportSG to more effectively administer its role in driving all Singaporeans to live better through sport.

committee-of-supply-head-u-prime-ministe.title: Committee of Supply debate on the Prime Minister's Office budget
committee-of-supply-head-u-prime-ministe.what_it_is: A Committee of Supply debate on Head U (Prime Minister's Office) of the Estimates, with MPs moving cuts and ministers responding on public service, research and innovation, climate policy, population, cash and banking access, and insurance.
committee-of-supply-head-u-prime-ministe.stage: Committee of Supply debate on Head U of the Estimates
committee-of-supply-head-u-prime-ministe.why_it_matters: The transcript states that the carbon tax has increased to $45 per tonne this year, that households will receive additional U-Save rebates to manage energy costs, and that HDB has given the go-ahead for DBS to set up an ATM at Rivervale Shores. It also records that MAS is monitoring cash acceptance and may consider making cash acceptance mandatory by law.

committee-of-supply-head-v-ministry-of-t.title: Committee of Supply debate on the Ministry of Trade and Industry budget
committee-of-supply-head-v-ministry-of-t.what_it_is: A Committee of Supply debate on Head V of the Ministry of Trade and Industry's budget, opened by a proposed $100 reduction and followed by Members' cuts and ministerial responses.
committee-of-supply-head-v-ministry-of-t.why_it_matters: The debate covers MTI's budget and policy directions, including support for SMEs, internationalisation, energy, and consumer protection. It records that public consultations on consumer protection will begin on 16 March 2026, and that the Government will reassess GDP and inflation forecasts if necessary. The record does not state that the specific proposals raised by Members were adopted.

expression-of-regret-at-the-conduct-of-m.title: Parliament debates and votes on motion on Pritam Singh's conduct and suitability as Leader of the Opposition
expression-of-regret-at-the-conduct-of-m.what_it_is: A motion moved by the Leader of the House asking Parliament to affirm honesty and integrity, note court and Committee of Privileges findings, express regret at Mr Pritam Singh's conduct, consider him unsuitable to continue as Leader of the Opposition, note implications for Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Faisal Manap, and call on MPs to uphold the law.
expression-of-regret-at-the-conduct-of-m.why_it_matters: The transcript states the Motion does not impose penalties or sanctions on Mr Pritam Singh under the PPIPA and does not itself remove the Leader of the Opposition; that designation is for the Prime Minister to decide. The House voted, the Ayes had it, and dissent was recorded for named Members. The Motion also asks the House to note that the High Court judgment and COP findings have implications for Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Faisal Manap, to be considered separately.

committee-of-supply-head-n-ministry-of-f.title: Committee of Supply debate on the Ministry of Foreign Affairs budget
committee-of-supply-head-n-ministry-of-f.what_it_is: A Committee of Supply debate on Head N, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, in which Mr Yip Hon Weng moved to reduce the total sum by $100 and Members questioned ministers on foreign policy.
committee-of-supply-head-n-ministry-of-f.why_it_matters: The record says foreign policy shapes Singapore's food security, energy resilience, jobs and safety abroad, and that supply-chain disruption affects jobs, cost of living and business confidence. It also records MFA consular assistance for Singaporeans overseas, including during emergencies.

an-artificial-intelligence-ai-transition.title: Motion on AI-enabled growth and support for workers and enterprises
an-artificial-intelligence-ai-transition.what_it_is: A Motion moved by Mr Ng Chee Meng setting out four commitments on AI-enabled economic growth, fairness, worker and enterprise support, and inclusive progress, followed by debate and a ministerial response.
an-artificial-intelligence-ai-transition.why_it_matters: The transcript sets out measures that affect workers and businesses: from the second half of this year, Singaporeans enrolled in selected SkillsFuture AI courses will receive six months of free access to premium AI tools; eligible businesses will receive $10,000 under the redesigned SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit later this year; and all IHLs will offer selected AI-related courses for alumni at a significant discount for a year starting in the second half of this year. It also records that the Government will study improvements to the SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support scheme and that tripartite partners are discussing shortening retrenchment notification under the Employment Act review.

reinforcing-singapore-s-position-as-a-gl.title: Motion on strengthening Singapore's economic competitiveness as a globally connected aviation, maritime and logistics hub
reinforcing-singapore-s-position-as-a-gl.what_it_is: A Motion moved by the Chairperson of the Government Parliamentary Committee for Transport, Ms Tin Pei Ling, affirming the importance of strengthening Singapore's long-term economic competitiveness through international cooperation, frontier technologies and world-class infrastructure, debated by Members and resolved by the House.
reinforcing-singapore-s-position-as-a-gl.why_it_matters: The transcript sets out concrete measures: MOT plans to invest $800 million over the next five years on transport research and innovation, and a manpower transition package for taxi and private-hire drivers includes place-and-train Career Conversion Programmes launching in the third quarter of this year, a $20-per-hour training incentive from January 2027, and a one-stop information webpage. Autonomous shuttles already run in Punggol and autonomous buses will be piloted on Service 400 in Marina Bay and Service 191 in One-North.

road-traffic-miscellaneous-amendments-bi.title: Second Reading of the Road Traffic (Miscellaneous Amendments) Bill
road-traffic-miscellaneous-amendments-bi.what_it_is: A Bill at Second Reading, moved by the Second Minister for Home Affairs on behalf of the Senior Minister, amending the Road Traffic Act to strengthen penalties for dangerous driving, tighten alcohol limits, create a drug-driving offence, and enhance enforcement.
road-traffic-miscellaneous-amendments-bi.why_it_matters: The Bill creates a new offence of purposeful endangerment carrying up to 15 years' imprisonment and lifetime disqualification, lowers the prescribed alcohol limits, makes holding a mobile phone while a vehicle is in motion an offence, and introduces a presence-based drug-driving offence. It also allows automated notices for traffic offences and tightens the Driver Improvement Points System from January 2027.

skills-and-workforce-development-agency-.title: Bill to merge SkillsFuture Singapore and Workforce Singapore into a new Skills and Workforce Development Agency
skills-and-workforce-development-agency-.what_it_is: A Bill at Second Reading to establish the Skills and Workforce Development Agency (SWDA) by merging SkillsFuture Singapore and Workforce Singapore and transferring their functions, employees and assets.
skills-and-workforce-development-agency-.why_it_matters: The Bill establishes SWDA as a statutory board whose functions cover the existing functions of SSG and WSG and extend to promoting career and employment services and training. If passed, SWDA will be established in the third quarter of 2026, and employees of WSG and SSG will transfer on terms no less favourable than their present ones. The Minister said SSG's and WSG's operations will be fully undertaken by SWDA from Day One, with existing grant and employment assistance commitments honoured.

committee-of-supply-head-x-ministry-of-c.title: Committee of Supply debate on MCCY and Muslim Affairs, ending with withdrawal of $100 reduction
committee-of-supply-head-x-ministry-of-c.what_it_is: A Committee of Supply debate on Head X of the Estimates for the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth, opened by Mr Alex Yam moving a $100 reduction and covering Muslim Affairs and MCCY clarifications.
committee-of-supply-head-x-ministry-of-c.why_it_matters: The transcript records planned changes to marriage and parenthood support, including expanding Bersamamu and making Project ARIF permanent from June 2026, and to education support through MENDAKI programmes and a Tampines after-school pilot. It also records mosque planning, the SCIS opening in 2028, WMS fundraising, and MCCY measures such as SpexSG taking effect from 1 April and SG Partnerships Fund co-funding. The record does not set out the full practical impact of every measure.

committee-of-supply-head-t-ministry-of-n.title: MND budget debate: housing, lift access, ageing estates and pest birds
committee-of-supply-head-t-ministry-of-n.what_it_is: A Committee of Supply debate on Head T of the Estimates for the Ministry of National Development, opened by Mr Henry Kwek moving a $100 reduction and ending with him seeking leave to withdraw the amendment.
committee-of-supply-head-t-ministry-of-n.why_it_matters: The debate covers HDB affordability, public rental, lift access, ageing estates, executive condominiums and pest birds. The transcript records that public rental has had no income ceiling since 2023, that HDB will look to implement lift access for 40 identified blocks within the next three years, and that a pigeon netting trial for 35 units will run from March to next March. Other proposals remain under review or without stated timelines.

committee-of-supply-head-o-ministry-of-h.title: Committee of Supply debate on the Ministry of Health budget
committee-of-supply-head-o-ministry-of-h.what_it_is: A Committee of Supply debate on Head O, Ministry of Health, including an amendment to reduce the allocation by $100 and ministerial responses on healthcare financing, preventive care, workforce and mental health.
committee-of-supply-head-o-ministry-of-h.why_it_matters: The Ministry announced higher MediSave withdrawal limits for chronic and preventive care from January 2027, subsidised genetic testing for hereditary breast and ovarian cancer from December this year, and extension of MediShield Life and MediSave to cover preventive surgeries for HBOC later this year. It also set out community health posts and specialist-supported care in Woodlands, and an AI risk assessment tool for Healthier SG enrolees from early 2027.

impact-of-the-middle-east-situation-on-s.title: Ministerial statements on the Middle East conflict and support measures for Singapore
impact-of-the-middle-east-situation-on-s.what_it_is: A series of ministerial statements addressing parliamentary questions on the impact of the Middle East situation on Singapore, followed by grouped clarifications from ministers.
impact-of-the-middle-east-situation-on-s.why_it_matters: The statements set out support measures including $200 cash for active platform workers, private hire car drivers and taxi drivers from the end of the month; enhanced U-Save rebates; $500 CDC vouchers brought forward to June 2026; and a $200 increase to the Budget 2026 Cost-of-Living Special Payment, with about 2.4 million Singaporeans receiving cash in September. They also state that the regulated electricity tariff is expected to rise more sharply in the next adjustment and that overall inflation for 2026 is expected to be higher than earlier projected.

committee-of-supply-head-w-ministry-of-t.title: Committee of Supply debate on transport spending and policy
committee-of-supply-head-w-ministry-of-t.what_it_is: A Committee of Supply debate on Head W of the Estimates, opened by Ms Tin Pei Ling moving a $100 reduction, followed by Member speeches and ministerial clarifications on transport policy.
committee-of-supply-head-w-ministry-of-t.why_it_matters: The transcript records a transport spending debate covering airport and port expansion, EV charging, autonomous vehicles, rail timelines, bus connectivity, road safety and COE reform. The only formal action is the withdrawal of the proposed $100 reduction in Head W, so the record does not show a spending change taking effect. The record does not set out the practical impact of the proposals beyond the stated questions and ministerial responses.

committee-of-supply-head-i-ministry-of-s.title: Committee of Supply debate on the Ministry of Social and Family Development budget
committee-of-supply-head-i-ministry-of-s.what_it_is: A Committee of Supply debate on the Ministry of Social and Family Development budget, opened by Mr Xie Yao Quan moving a $100 reduction to Head I of the Estimates, with MPs raising policy asks and ministers setting out MSF plans.
committee-of-supply-head-i-ministry-of-s.why_it_matters: The transcript sets out changes including a new $500 quarterly Partnership Payout for all ComLink+ families, a rise in the Student Care Fee Assistance income threshold from $4,500 to $6,500 benefiting around 13,000 students, and from January 2027 a higher gross monthly household income ceiling of $15,000 for childcare and Kindergarten Fee Assistance. It also states that from July 2026 subsidies for residential and community disability services will rise by up to 15 and 10 percentage points, and that filing Form 1 of an LPA will be free for citizens.

veterinary-practice-bill.title: Veterinary Practice Bill at Second Reading, creating a Veterinary Council to register and discipline vets
veterinary-practice-bill.what_it_is: A Bill at Second Reading, moved by the Minister of State for National Development on behalf of the Minister for National Development, that establishes a Veterinary Council to register veterinarians and regulate the practice of veterinary medicine in Singapore.
veterinary-practice-bill.why_it_matters: The Minister said vets will have to be registered with the new Council and hold a valid practising certificate to practise, and that the Registrar must publish registered vets' particulars so the public can search for and verify a vet's registration status and place of practice. The maximum financial penalty for unlawful practice or misrepresentation as a vet rises from $10,000 to $50,000. Existing AVS-licensed vets will be temporarily deemed duly qualified and must obtain registration and a practising certificate within a stipulated grace period to continue practising.

committee-of-supply-head-j-ministry-of-d.title: MINDEF budget debate and withdrawn $100 amendment
committee-of-supply-head-j-ministry-of-d.what_it_is: A Committee of Supply debate on Head J (Ministry of Defence) of the Estimates, in which Mr Yip Hon Weng moved and later withdrew an amendment to reduce the allocation by $100.
committee-of-supply-head-j-ministry-of-d.stage: Committee of Supply debate on Head J of the Estimates
committee-of-supply-head-j-ministry-of-d.why_it_matters: The Minister said MINDEF/SAF will build a suite of conventional, cheap-asymmetric, cyber and classified capabilities, acquire three Gulfstream G550 maritime surveillance aircraft, and scale unmanned platforms paired with manned platforms. He also said MINDEF will take care of NSmen and NSFs in consultation with the Ministry of Finance where budget space allows, regularly review NSF allowances, and do more for HOME awards, NS credits and tax incentives where possible. The debate also covered cross-domain cooperation with other agencies and new international partnerships on cyber, information warfare and critical underwater infrastructure.

committee-of-supply-head-l-ministry-of-s.title: Committee of Supply debate on the Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment budget
committee-of-supply-head-l-ministry-of-s.what_it_is: A Committee of Supply debate on Head L of the Estimates for the Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment, covering climate adaptation, water, food, heat, waste and related policies.
committee-of-supply-head-l-ministry-of-s.stage: Committee of Supply debate on Head L of the Estimates
committee-of-supply-head-l-ministry-of-s.why_it_matters: The transcript states that from April the Beverage Container Return Scheme will add a 10-cent deposit on marked beverage containers, refundable at reverse vending machines, and that climate vouchers will be expanded next month to include five-tick clothes dryers and induction stoves. It also states that 2026 is designated the Year of Climate Adaptation, that a National Adaptation Plan will be published in 2027, and that portable flood barriers and flood alerts are being made available to residents.

committee-of-supply-head-p-ministry-of-h.title: Committee of Supply debate on Ministry of Home Affairs Head P
committee-of-supply-head-p-ministry-of-h.what_it_is: A Committee of Supply debate on Head P of the Estimates for the Ministry of Home Affairs, opened by a proposed $100 reduction and followed by Members' speeches and ministerial responses.
committee-of-supply-head-p-ministry-of-h.stage: Committee of Supply (Head P of the Estimates)
committee-of-supply-head-p-ministry-of-h.why_it_matters: The debate covers Home Team policies on terrorism, cyberattacks, drugs, scams, rehabilitation, fire safety and road safety. The transcript states specific changes including extending Fire Certificate validity from one year to three years from 1 April 2026, planning to bring RHA measures into force by end-2026, and amending FICA to allow anticipatory directions against online communications.

committee-of-supply-head-q-ministry-of-d.title: Committee of Supply debate on MDDI Head Q: AI adoption, online safety and cybersecurity
committee-of-supply-head-q-ministry-of-d.what_it_is: A Committee of Supply debate on the Ministry of Digital Development and Information's Head Q budget, opened by Mr Sharael Taha moving a $100 reduction and followed by ministerial responses.
committee-of-supply-head-q-ministry-of-d.why_it_matters: The debate covers measures intended to help more local enterprises adopt AI, with the National AI Impact Programme aiming to support 10,000 local enterprises over three years. It also covers online safety, scam and misinformation risks, and a planned AI translation tool to make public-facing materials more accessible to non-English speakers. The record does not quantify the effect on households or individual workers beyond these stated aims.

national-council-of-social-service-amend.title: Second Reading of the National Council of Social Service (Amendment) Bill
national-council-of-social-service-amend.what_it_is: A Bill at Second Reading to amend the National Council of Social Service Act, moved by the Minister for Social and Family Development, updating NCSS's objectives, membership, Council governance and related statutory provisions.
national-council-of-social-service-amend.why_it_matters: The Bill updates NCSS's statutory objectives and functions to strengthen social service delivery, build sector capabilities and develop the broader social service ecosystem. It introduces a single-tier sector membership and a fully appointed Council, and extends ComChest's role beyond fundraising. The record says these changes are intended to improve outcomes for service users and support those in need.
